intended_object: The pairing map into a product of preorders: given monotone maps f_i : α → π_i, it is the monotone map α → Π_i π_i sending x to (f_i(x))_i. This is the universal property of the product of preorders, as stated in the docstring.
explanation: The underlying function sends x to the family `fun i => f i x`. Its monotonicity follows from the monotonicity of each f_i, together with the pointwise order on the Pi type. This is exactly the standard construction. On generality: `OrderHom` is defined in Mathlib only for preorders, and the index family is arbitrary, so the construction is already at the generality of the bundled `→o` API. The declaration is itself part of Mathlib, so there is no separate Mathlib counterpart to cite.
